parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks universal exposures: federal document rules barring X/mismatched markers, entry cable directing refusal on sex doubt with possible lifetime fraud findings, federal facility bans, and a state law (in force 4 Dec 2025) requiring birth-certificate-sex restroom use across state buildings, schools and prisons — enforced with ID checks and one documented arrest, with the trans woman held 24 hours in a men's ward. The state sits in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier. Custody adds documented harm (surgery denial upheld; federal conversion-therapy policy). Mitigants — federal employment/hate-crime protections, enjoining courts, legal aid, city ordinances — are partial and do not reach the operative exclusions.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 bar on X/mismatched markers; Nov 2025 Supreme Court allowed restrictions; reports of confiscated/blocked passports stranding travellers; cable directs refusal where sex is in doubt and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; litigation by civil-liberties union pending; fraud finding requires four elements, limited waiver, never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Border refusal → document discrepancy → possible fraud referral → detention/state custody exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman arrested 19 Mar 2025 under a restroom statute (60-day misdemeanour), held 24h in men's ward; state corrections deny transition surgery (appeals court upheld); federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policy from 2026; immigration custody reports of beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Facility offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; prison statute covers restrooms only, not cell assignment; federal courts enjoined several orders.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Restroom ID check → arrest → birth-sex placement → custody care denial.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from funded single-sex facilities; 22 state/provinces restrict facilities, 4 criminalise in some circumstances; this state's law reaches schools, universities, prisons, state buildings with $25k/$125k fines; enforcement began days after 4 Dec 2025 with trooper ID checks.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 units and the capital have no mapped ban; some cities have protections.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State ban + federal funding leverage + DOJ school-district investigation escalated Apr 2026.

care_services.exposure: State banned youth gender-affirming care (2023); DOJ 2022 opinion classifying it as child abuse; subpoenas of under-19 patient records; proposed federal rule barring insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; crisis-lifeline LGBTQ services shut.
care_services.protection: Adult care not documented as banned; some city and federal employment protections survive; courts blocked several orders.
care_services.interaction: Travelling family with a trans minor faces care denial plus investigation risk under federal and state directives.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist framings; governor directed recognition of two genders only; officials' arrest described as deliberate humiliation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward is not keyed to gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; courts and press constrain rhetoric.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing lowers police discretion floor and raises outing consequences at every checkpoint.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directing criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; parental-rights statute (Jun 2025) mandates misgendering in schools; youth care banned; school bathroom policy under DOJ investigation.
minors_guardians.protection: Enjoinment litigation pending; five DAs refused earlier directives; injunctions blocked some family-services investigations.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling parent with a trans minor encounters school/facility rules and record-subpoena risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025; state hate-crime statute omits gender identity and prosecutions are rare; no statewide nondiscrimination law; LGB visibility rolling back (rescinded ordinance, suspended Pride).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 2020 federal employment ruling recognised in state courts; city ordinances protect.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak state recourse shifts burden to federal mechanisms with uneven uptake.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Top 'Do Not Travel' tier (Jul 2026) graded law-by-law; unclear enforcement guidance produces uneven, invasive checks; document-renewal status after Sep 2025 act unsourced; school investigation outcome unknown; general homicide baseline absent, so violence rate uncalibrated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Running legal-aid FAQ; several federal orders blocked or enjoined; ongoing passport litigation; national equality and identity-document maps track changes.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Contested federal posture makes exposure time-of-travel dependent and hard to predict.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Ostravia, this state imposes birth-sex facility rules with a criminal statute and slow remedies. It rates lower because exposure also runs at the federal border (marker refusal, fraud referral) and custody harm is documented (men's-ward holding, surgery denial upheld, conversion-therapy policy).

Karthovia's police ID stops, hours of questioning and nuisance fines resemble this state's restroom ID checks. This case is lower: the conduct is statutory, backed by imprisonment exposure, official threat-framing and a Do-Not-Travel grade, not merely discretionary harassment with detention rare.

Saruth's prolonged border cells, withheld care and illusory habeas are far grimmer. Here remedies partially function — courts enjoin orders, litigation proceeds, entry refusal is administrative rather than weeks in custody — so this sits materially above the 0.15 tier.

Kestrel Isles' discretionary secondary screening with refused admission and slow appeals captures the entry axis alone. This jurisdiction layers facility criminalisation, custody placement harm and state hostility on top, so it rates well below this administrative-friction anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one system: federal document and entry rules make outing near-universal at the border (X markers stopped, discrepancy-driven refusal, possible fraud finding), while the state's Dec 2025 birth-certificate restroom law extends that exposure to every state building, school and prison, with documented enforcement and an arrest ending in a men's-ward hold. Custody multiplies severity — surgery denial upheld federally, a conversion-therapy-style federal corrections policy, immigration custody abuse reports. State recourse is thin: no gender-identity hate-crime or nondiscrimination coverage, and a top 'Do Not Travel' grade. Federal protections (employment ruling, hate-crime statute, enjoining courts, legal aid) prevent a lower tier but do not reach the operative exclusions, so risk sits in the 0.25–0.30 range.
